data.title: Disney Hit With Lawsuit Alleging Unlicensed Social Media Music
data.summary: The latest in a flood of lawsuits over music on social media is targeting the Walt Disney Co. — and claiming that the Hollywood giant should have known better. In a case filed Tuesday (Nov. 24) in Detroit federal court, Zac Hiller and his LAA Music claim Disney illegally used three of the publishing company’s songs across seven social media videos even though the entertainment colossus “never asked for a license” and “never paid a dollar.” [...] Disney Sued for Allegedly Using Unlicensed Music in Social Media Ads: ‘Never Paid a Dollar’ The new case is one of dozens brought against brands over music on Instagram and TikTok, but none have targeted a media giant like Disney. The Walt Disney logo is displayed on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange during morning trading on October 21, 2026 in New York City. [...] “For a hundred years, The Walt Disney Company has taught the world one rule: if you want to use what someone else created, you ask permission and you pay,” Hiller’s attorneys write. “Disney enforces that rule against everyone else. This case is about Disney exempting itself from it.”
